name: Axolotl
where: Regina Jones's reward for her last Watson gig, Last Call (since 2.1 it replaces the old NeoFiber; Tier 5 if you are level 33+). Also sold by Dogtown ripperdocs (Phantom Liberty) and in the Airdrops, as an iconic implant. Tiers: 4 to 5++.
effect: Each kill cuts the cooldown of all your cyberware by 5–7.5%. Update 2.1 lowered both the reduction and its capacity cost. The iconic version of the Newton Module.
verdict: For builds that chain kills with Sandevistan, Berserk or quickhacks: free from Regina's gigs.

name: Bioconductor
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: Quickhacks can crit: 15–35% quickhack Crit Chance, at the cost of −4 Max RAM. COX-2 is its iconic version.
verdict: For damage netrunners who already have RAM to spare.

name: Camillo RAM Manager
where: Any ripperdoc from level 30. Tiers: 4 to 5++.
effect: When your RAM drops to 15–20%, restores 20–23% of Max RAM; +2 Max RAM. Cooldown 80 s. Update 2.1 cut its cooldown and capacity cost. RAM Reallocator is its iconic version.
verdict: For netrunners from level 30: very cheap in capacity.

name: COX-2 Cybersomatic Optimizer
where: Dogtown ripperdocs (Phantom Liberty) and Airdrops: one of the 15 iconic implants the repeating Airdrops guarantee (they start in Lucretia My Reflection). Tiers: 3 to 5++.
effect: Iconic Bioconductor: quickhacks get 80–100% Crit Chance, at the cost of −8 to −4 Max RAM.
verdict: For the late-game damage netrunner with Phantom Liberty; heavy on capacity.

name: Ex-Disk
where: Any ripperdoc from level 20. Tiers: 3 to 5++.
effect: +4–6 Max RAM and +20–35% quickhack upload speed. Update 2.1 raised its upload bonus.
verdict: The plainest RAM boost for any netrunner from level 20.

name: Kerenzikov Boost System
where: Any ripperdoc from level 20. Tiers: 3 to 5. (Sources disagree: the game files start it at Tier 1.)
effect: While Kerenzikov is active, shooting costs no Stamina and time slows a further 5–15%. Without Kerenzikov (Nervous System) installed it does nothing (inference).
verdict: Only for Kerenzikov gunfighters; almost free in capacity.

name: Mechatronic Core
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5.
effect: +15–40% damage against drones, robots, mechs and turrets; +1–2 Max RAM.
verdict: Cheap and handy for anyone fighting Militech, Arasaka or Barghest machines.

name: Memory Boost
where: Any ripperdoc from level 5 per the wiki (unverified: it is Tier 2, which other pages tie to level 10). Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Each kill returns 0.4–1.25 RAM; +1 Max RAM.
verdict: For netrunners who finish enemies with guns between hacks.

name: Newton Module
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1 per game8's list (the wiki gives no acquisition text; unverified). Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: Each kill cuts the cooldown of all your cyberware by 0.3–1.35%. The non-iconic Axolotl.
verdict: A low-cost Axolotl for the early game.

name: Quantum Tuner
where: Songbird path of Phantom Liberty only: in From Her to Eternity, inside the hidden container at Tranquil Terrace. Not sold. Tiers: 5 to 5++.
effect: When another implant is used up, it resets that cooldown (up to 30–50 s); its own cooldown is 60 s. Passive: −10–15% cooldown on all cyberware.
verdict: For Sandevistan or Berserk builds that trigger often; lost if you side with Reed.

name: RAM Reallocator
where: Dogtown ripperdocs (Phantom Liberty) and Airdrops: one of the 15 iconic implants the repeating Airdrops guarantee (they start in Lucretia My Reflection). Tiers: 3 to 5++. (The game files start it at Tier 4.)
effect: When your RAM drops to 15–20%, restores 30–45% of Max RAM; +2 Max RAM; cooldown 95–85 s. Sources disagree: the cyberware overview says 20–23%; 2.1 raised the recovered RAM, so the higher figure looks current (inference). Iconic Camillo RAM Manager.
verdict: For late-game netrunners who empty their RAM every fight.

name: RAM Upgrade
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: +0.05–0.2 RAM regen per second and +1–2 Max RAM. Update 2.1 raised the regen.
verdict: The first cortex implant for a new netrunner.

name: Self-ICE
where: Any ripperdoc from level 20. Tiers: 3 to 5++. In Phantom Liberty, Nix gives you one in Black Steel in the Hour of Chaos if you did KOLD MIRAGE and Spellbound with Nix alive.
effect: Automatically blocks one enemy quickhack; +1–2 Max RAM. Cooldown 45–20 s.
verdict: For everyone from level 20: almost free and it stops enemy netrunners.

name: Arasaka Mk.1–Mk.5
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++. In game it is just "Arasaka"; "Arasaka Shadow" is the game-file name and the wiki page title.
effect: RAM 5–9, 4–8 quickhack slots, buffer 0–4. Tier 2: enemies take 40% longer to trace you. Tier 3: −2 RAM on Covert quickhacks. Tier 4: +5 RAM on a takedown. Tier 5: in Overclock, quickhacks add no trace.
verdict: The stealth netrunner's cyberdeck (inference from its bonuses).

name: Biotech Σ Mk.1–Mk.4
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++. In Phantom Liberty a scripted Airdrop in the parking lot by the Akebono Hotel (Luxor Heights) holds one at Tier 3 to 5+.
effect: RAM 6–9, 5–8 slots, buffer 1–4. Tier 2: +15–60% Combat quickhack duration. Tier 3: +10% quickhack damage over time. Tier 4: +25% Monowire damage against targets taking damage over time. Tier 5: Overclock refreshes damage-over-time effects.
verdict: For Contagion and Overheat netrunners.

name: Militech Canto Mk.6
where: Crafted only: the spec is in the Cynosure Experimental Prototyping lab (Sector 3, keycode 714212) in Somewhat Damaged, and you also need the Cerberus behavioral component decoded by Yoko (This Corrosion). Reed path only, and it is this **or** the Erebus SMG, not both. Tiers: 5 to 5++ (the game files start it at Tier 3).
effect: Iconic talking cyberdeck (a rogue AI voice): RAM 10, 4 slots, buffer 4, and it unlocks the Blackwall Gateway quickhack.
verdict: For the Reed-path netrunner who picks Blackwall Gateway over the Erebus.

name: Militech Paraline Mk.1–Mk.5
where: Every V owns a Tier 1 Paraline from The Rescue; higher tiers at any ripperdoc. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: RAM 5–9, 4–8 slots, buffer 0–4. Tier 2: +10% quickhack damage. Tier 3: Monowire +2% damage per RAM used. Tier 4: Smart weapon hits speed up uploads. Tier 5: in Overclock, Smart weapons and Monowire deal bonus Electrical damage.
verdict: For players mixing Smart weapons or Monowire with quickhacks.

name: NetWatch Netdriver Mk.1
where: Any ripperdoc from level 40. Tiers: 5 to 5++. The wiki flags it as iconic. Before 2.0 it was the "Mk.5" (obsolete name).
effect: RAM 13, 8 slots, buffer 4. −20% trace when hacking through cameras, −50% RAM on device and vehicle quickhacks, and +15–30% damage on Combat quickhacks sent through devices.
verdict: The deck with the highest base RAM: the goal of any netrunner at level 40.

name: Raven Microcyber Mk.1–Mk.3
where: Any ripperdoc from level 20. Tiers: 3 to 5++. A pre-2.0 Mk.4 no longer exists.
effect: RAM 7–9, 6–8 slots, buffer 2–4 (sources disagree: the overview says 5–8 slots and buffer 6–8). Tier 3: +40–100% spread range. Tier 4: quickhacks spread instantly. Tier 5: in Overclock, 15% chance to spread to two more enemies.
verdict: For netrunners who clear groups with spreading hacks such as Contagion.

name: Tetratronic Rippler Mk.1–Mk.4
where: Any ripperdoc. Tiers: 1 to 5++. In Phantom Liberty, the first Airdrop (Wild Blue Hotel, behind the Akebono, during Lucretia My Reflection) holds one at Tier 3 to 5+.
effect: RAM 5–20 (with the Tier 4+ bonus), 4–8 slots, buffer 1–4. Tier 2: +15% weapon damage against enemies not hit by Combat quickhacks. Tier 3: +40% to a Combat quickhack that follows a non-Combat one. Tier 5: Overclock auto-uploads Reboot Optics and Weapon Glitch within 8 m. Sources disagree on the Tier 4 Max RAM bonus (+5/8/12 or +4/7).
verdict: For the hybrid who hacks and shoots; free in Phantom Liberty.

name: Dynalar Sandevistan
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5.
effect: Toggled on and off: slows time 50% and gives +5–15% Crit Chance and Crit Damage. Lasts 8 s; cooldown 55 s.
verdict: For crit-hunting gunfighters from level 10.

name: Militech "Apogee" Sandevistan
where: Any ripperdoc from level 40. Tiers: 5 only. Iconic.
effect: Activates at any charge: slows time 85% and gives +15–20% headshot damage, Crit Chance and Crit Damage. Each kill extends it by 10% and gives +22% Stamina. Lasts 6 s; cooldown 30–25 s. Update 2.1 shortened it but raised its bonuses.
verdict: The endgame Sandevistan for Reflexes builds; save up for it.

name: Militech "Falcon" Sandevistan
where: Any ripperdoc from level 30. Tiers: 4 to 5. In Phantom Liberty, Carol Emeka gives it to you in Black Steel in the Hour of Chaos if you asked her to help against MaxTac. Sources disagree on whether it is iconic (the infobox says yes, the text does not).
effect: Activates at any charge: slows time 70%, +5–10% damage and +5–15% Crit Chance; each kill extends it by 5% and heals 10–12% Health. Lasts 9–10 s; cooldown 40–30 s.
verdict: A long, self-healing Sandevistan for level 30, before you can afford the Apogee.

name: QianT "Warp Dancer" Sandevistan
where: Any ripperdoc from level 20. Tiers: 3 to 5.
effect: Defensive Sandevistan: only a 20% time slow, but +14–24% Mitigation Chance, +7–15% Mitigation Strength and +30–60% elemental resistance. Lasts 9–10 s; cooldown 70–40 s.
verdict: For players who want toughness more than slow-motion; cheap in capacity.

name: Zetatech Sandevistan
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5. In Phantom Liberty it is also the reward from Gig: Prototype in the Scraper.
effect: Slows time 30% and gives +3–12% damage; in midair, 60% slow, +6–24% damage and +25–40% headshot damage. Lasts 6 s; cooldown 45 s.
verdict: For airborne builds with double jump or Air Dash.

name: BioDyne Berserk
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5.
effect: Active 8–11 s: +30–50% damage reduction, Health cannot drop below 25%, melee only, +15–30% attack speed, +5–20% Crit Chance and +100% Crit Damage. Cooldown 60–35 s. Update 2.1 added the damage reduction and fixed the bug that kept Health above 25% at all times.
verdict: The offensive Berserk for blade or Gorilla Arms builds.

name: Militech Berserk
where: Any ripperdoc from level 30. Tiers: 4 to 5. Iconic. If you don't own it, the endings listed in the wiki's endings table give it to you (Legendary).
effect: Active 11–12 s: invulnerable, melee only, +25–30% attack speed, +15–20% movement speed and up to +50% damage at low Health. Cooldown 40–25 s.
verdict: The best Berserk for Body melee builds from level 30.

name: Moore Tech Berserk
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5.
effect: Active 8–11 s: +30–50% damage reduction, Health cannot drop below 25%, melee only, attacks cost no Stamina; when it ends you heal 25% Health per kill. Cooldown 60–25 s.
verdict: The cheapest Berserk (12 capacity): the one to start a melee build with.

name: Zetatech Berserk
where: Any ripperdoc from level 30 per the wiki (sources disagree: it is Tier 3, normally sold from level 20). Tiers: 3 to 5.
effect: Active 9–11 s: +35–50% damage reduction, Health cannot drop below 25%, melee only, +10–20% attack speed and −20–30% fall damage. Cooldown 45–25 s.
verdict: The tankiest Berserk, for melee builds that dive in from above.

name: Chrome Compressor
where: Dogtown ripperdocs (Phantom Liberty) and Airdrops: one of the 15 iconic implants the repeating Airdrops guarantee (they start in Lucretia My Reflection). Tiers: 2 to 5++. Psycho Killer's infobox also lists it as Regina's final reward, but the implant's page does not and a 2.3 bug note says it may not be given (sources disagree).
effect: Takes the Operating System slot with no active ability: costs 0 capacity and adds +40–70 Cyberware Capacity. With it the reachable maximum is 430 (360 without). game8 still says +42, a pre-2.1 figure.
verdict: For gun or passive builds that use no cyberdeck, Sandevistan or Berserk.

name: Electrifying Gorilla Arms
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Blunt arm weapon: Electrical damage, 10–20% Shock chance, and +1–6 to Body checks. Since 2.5, Glamdocs can restyle it.
verdict: For Body builds: blunt hits and help with strength checks.

name: Electrifying Mantis Blades
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Arm blades with a leap attack: Electrical damage, 10–20% Shock chance. Since 2.5, Glamdocs can restyle them.
verdict: For Reflexes and blade builds: the leap closes distance.

name: Electrifying Monowire
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Mid-range whip that hits several enemies: Electrical damage, 10–20% Shock chance, and one quickhack slot (Control hacks only with the Jailbreak Relic perk).
verdict: For netrunners who want a melee weapon with a quickhack built in.

name: Electrifying Projectile Launch System
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Arm-mounted launcher; the charged shot deals +30% damage with +25% radius and +100% Stun (Electrical damage). Shares its button with grenades and Optical Camo.
verdict: For Technical Ability builds who want a launcher always at hand.

name: Gorilla Arms
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++. If you lack a pair, the endings in the wiki's table give you Legendary ones (Path of Least Resistance gives nothing).
effect: Blunt arm weapon: Physical damage, 10–20% Bleed chance, and +1–6 to Body checks. Since 2.5, Glamdocs can restyle it.
verdict: For Body builds: blunt hits and help with strength checks.

name: Mantis Blades
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Arm blades with a leap attack: Physical damage, 10–20% Bleed chance. Since 2.5, Glamdocs can restyle them. Gang and corp cosmetic styles exist.
verdict: For Reflexes and blade builds: the leap closes distance.

name: MaxTac Mantis Blades
where: Missable, Reed path only: in Black Steel in the Hour of Chaos hire Yoko (€$15,000), accept her proposal and send Mr. Hands the coordinates; the gift arrives after Leave in Silence. Melissa Rory also drops them if you kill her after Bullets. Tiers: 4 to 5++.
effect: Arm blades with a leap attack: Physical damage, 10–20% Bleed chance. Since 2.5, Glamdocs can restyle them. MaxTac variant that starts at Tier 4, with 15–20% Bleed.
verdict: Mantis Blades that start at Tier 4: worth it on the Reed path.

name: Monowire
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Mid-range whip that hits several enemies: Physical damage, 10–20% Bleed chance, and one quickhack slot (Control hacks only with the Jailbreak Relic perk). The longest-reach melee weapon in the game. (Before 1.5 it scaled with Cool: obsolete.)
verdict: For netrunners who want a melee weapon with a quickhack built in.

name: Projectile Launch System
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Arm-mounted launcher; the charged shot deals +30% damage with +25% radius and +40% dismemberment. Shares its button with grenades and Optical Camo.
verdict: For Technical Ability builds who want a launcher always at hand.

name: Thermal Gorilla Arms
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Blunt arm weapon: Thermal damage, 10–20% Burn chance, and +1–6 to Body checks. Since 2.5, Glamdocs can restyle it.
verdict: For Body builds: blunt hits and help with strength checks.

name: Thermal Mantis Blades
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Arm blades with a leap attack: Thermal damage, 10–20% Burn chance. Since 2.5, Glamdocs can restyle them.
verdict: For Reflexes and blade builds: the leap closes distance.

name: Thermal Monowire
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Mid-range whip that hits several enemies: Thermal damage, 10–20% Burn chance, and one quickhack slot (Control hacks only with the Jailbreak Relic perk).
verdict: For netrunners who want a melee weapon with a quickhack built in.

name: Thermal Projectile Launch System
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Arm-mounted launcher; the charged shot deals +30% damage with +25% radius and +30% Burn. Shares its button with grenades and Optical Camo.
verdict: For Technical Ability builds who want a launcher always at hand.

name: Toxic Gorilla Arms
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Blunt arm weapon: Chemical damage, 10–20% Poison chance, and +1–6 to Body checks. Since 2.5, Glamdocs can restyle it.
verdict: For Body builds: blunt hits and help with strength checks.

name: Toxic Mantis Blades
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Arm blades with a leap attack: Chemical damage, 10–20% Poison chance. Since 2.5, Glamdocs can restyle them.
verdict: For Reflexes and blade builds: the leap closes distance.

name: Toxic Monowire
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Mid-range whip that hits several enemies: Chemical damage, 10–20% Poison chance, and one quickhack slot (Control hacks only with the Jailbreak Relic perk).
verdict: For netrunners who want a melee weapon with a quickhack built in.

name: Toxic Projectile Launch System
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Arm-mounted launcher; the charged shot deals +30% damage with +25% radius and +30% Poison. Shares its button with grenades and Optical Camo.
verdict: For Technical Ability builds who want a launcher always at hand.

name: Bionic Joints
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: Armor 25–130, nothing else.
verdict: Cheap, plain armor for any build.

name: Dense Marrow
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Armor 18–54; +15–27% melee damage, but melee attacks cost 20% more Stamina. Update 2.1 lowered its Armor and raised the Stamina cost.
verdict: For melee builds that manage their Stamina.

name: Epimorphic Skeleton
where: Any ripperdoc from level 30. Tiers: 4 to 5++.
effect: Armor 96–186 and +10–13% Max Health. Update 2.1 lowered its Armor.
verdict: For tanks from level 30 with capacity to spare.

name: Feen-X
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: Armor 8–38; +250% RAM regen when you have less than 3–7 RAM left. Added in Update 2.1.
verdict: For netrunners who drain their RAM every fight.

name: Kinetic Frame
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: Armor 17–117; +8–18% Mitigation Chance while your Stamina is above 85%.
verdict: For gunfighters who spend little Stamina.

name: Para Bellum
where: Any ripperdoc from level 20. Tiers: 3 to 5++. (Sources disagree: the game files start it at Tier 1.)
effect: Armor 30–150 and +8–12% Armor. Rara Avis is its iconic version.
verdict: For any build that wants more Armor from level 20.

name: RAM Recoup
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: Armor 10–46; taking damage restores RAM (0.2–0.3% of the damage); +1–2 Max RAM.
verdict: For netrunners who fight up close.

name: Rara Avis
where: Dogtown ripperdocs (Phantom Liberty) and Airdrops: one of the 15 iconic implants the repeating Airdrops guarantee (they start in Lucretia My Reflection). Tiers: 3 to 5++. (The game files start it at Tier 4.)
effect: Iconic Para Bellum: +30–40% Armor. Update 2.1 cut its capacity cost.
verdict: For late-game tanks with Phantom Liberty.

name: Scar Coalescer
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: Armor 10–46; +10–22% Armor below 50% Health.
verdict: For builds that fight at low Health.

name: Scarab
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: Armor 10–46; while crouched, +30–130 Armor and −20% movement speed.
verdict: For snipers and stealth players who spend their time crouched.

name: Spring Joints
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++. (Sources disagree: the game files start it at Tier 1.)
effect: Armor 18–46; +10–18% Mitigation Strength (90% cap).
verdict: For Reflexes builds stacking mitigation.

name: Titanium Bones
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: Armor 10–46; +30–66% carrying capacity.
verdict: For players who pick up all the loot to sell.

name: Universal Booster
where: Any ripperdoc from level 20. Tiers: 3 to 5++. (Sources disagree: the game files start it at Tier 1.)
effect: Armor 90–186; health items also give +5–10% Armor and −15–30% Stamina costs for 5 s. The wiki says it stacks since 2.1; game8 says it does not (a pre-2.1 source).
verdict: For builds that heal a lot mid-fight.

name: Adrenaline Converter
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: +20–40% movement speed for 3–9 s on entering combat.
verdict: Cheap pick for melee builds that need to close in.

name: Adreno-trigger
where: Dogtown ripperdocs (Phantom Liberty) and Airdrops: one of the 15 iconic implants the repeating Airdrops guarantee (they start in Lucretia My Reflection). Tiers: 3 to 5++.
effect: Iconic Adrenaline Converter: +20–30% movement speed for 10–35 s on entering combat. Update 2.1 shortened it.
verdict: For Phantom Liberty melee builds.

name: Atomic Sensors
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: Out of combat, movement speed rises with enemy detection (up to +20–64%).
verdict: For stealth players who want to slip away when spotted.

name: Deep-field Visual Interface
where: Dogtown ripperdocs (Phantom Liberty) and Airdrops: one of the 15 iconic implants the repeating Airdrops guarantee (they start in Lucretia My Reflection). Tiers: 3 to 5++. (The game files have it at Tier 5 only.)
effect: Iconic Visual Cortex Support: Crit Chance rises with distance, up to +70–100% at 85–100 m.
verdict: For Phantom Liberty snipers.

name: Kerenzikov
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Aiming or shooting while sliding, dodging or Dashing slows time 60% for 2–3.75 s. Cooldown 8–6 s. Kerenzikov Boost System and Defenzikov rely on it (inference).
verdict: For agile Reflexes gunfighters: the first big implant at level 10.

name: NeoFiber
where: Any ripperdoc from level 20. Tiers: 3 to 5++. (Sources disagree: the game files start it at Tier 2.)
effect: +8–11% Mitigation Chance and +5–11% Mitigation Strength.
verdict: Passive defense for any build.

name: Reflex Tuner
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: Below 25% Health, slows time 20–60% for 2–4.5 s. Cooldown 60–35 s. Revulsor is its iconic version.
verdict: Cheap insurance for tight spots.

name: Revulsor
where: Dogtown ripperdocs (Phantom Liberty) and Airdrops: one of the 15 iconic implants the repeating Airdrops guarantee (they start in Lucretia My Reflection). Tiers: 3 to 5++.
effect: Iconic Reflex Tuner: below 25% Health, slows time 40–60% for 3.5–4.5 s and you are not slowed. Cooldown 50–35 s.
verdict: For builds that live on the edge of their Health bar.

name: Stabber
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: +10–20% Crit Chance with blades and throwables.
verdict: For knife and katana builds.

name: Synaptic Accelerator
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: When enemy detection hits 50%, slows time 20–50% for 2–4.5 s. Cooldown 60 s.
verdict: For stealth players: buys time to hide or knock out.

name: Tyrosine Injector
where: Any ripperdoc. Tiers: 1 to 5++. A free one sits in a cache at the Assault in Progress on Pinewood St (Kabuki, southeast of the No-Tell Motel).
effect: After a takedown: +10–21% headshot damage and +5–11% movement speed for 15 s.
verdict: For stealth players who take one down, then shoot the rest.

name: Visual Cortex Support
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: Crit Chance rises with distance, up to +16–30% at 30 m. Deep-field Visual Interface is its iconic version.
verdict: For precision and sniper rifle users.

name: Carapace
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Armor 38–94; +20–32% Armor effectiveness against attacks from the side or rear.
verdict: For players who dive into crowds.

name: Cellular Adapter
where: Any ripperdoc. Tiers: 2 to 5++. You need the Built Different perk (Technical Ability) to install it.
effect: Armor 74–162; per Technical Ability point: +1% explosion resistance, +0.5% Tech weapon damage and +0.5% health item and grenade recharge.
verdict: For high Technical Ability builds.

name: Chitin
where: Dogtown ripperdocs (Phantom Liberty) and Airdrops: one of the 15 iconic implants the repeating Airdrops guarantee (they start in Lucretia My Reflection). Tiers: 3 to 5++. (The game files have it at Tier 5 only.)
effect: Iconic Subdermal Armor: Armor 140–200 and extra Health regen.
verdict: For late-game tanks with capacity to spare.

name: Cogito Lattice
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: Armor 18–54; +200–240% of its Armor when you have less than 2–10 RAM left. Added in Update 2.1.
verdict: Armor for netrunners.

name: Countershell
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: Armor 17–57; if you lose 35% Health within 3 s, +30–50% Mitigation Chance for 4 s.
verdict: Cheap insurance against burst damage.

name: Defenzikov
where: Any ripperdoc from level 20. Tiers: 3 to 5++.
effect: Armor 24–80; +50–90% Mitigation Chance for 3–4 s after Kerenzikov ends. Needs Kerenzikov (inference).
verdict: Kerenzikov builds only.

name: Nano-plating
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Armor 38–78; 4–7% chance to block projectiles (+100% right after a dodge or Dash). Update 2.1 moved its attunement from Cool to Reflexes.
verdict: For Reflexes builds that dodge a lot.

name: Optical Camo
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++. The figures on the wiki's "Pre-2.0 Update" subpage are obsolete.
effect: Armor 15–30; −30–90% visibility for 4–7 s. Cooldown 70–50 s. Shares the grenade and Projectile Launch System button.
verdict: The core stealth implant, from level 10.

name: Pain Editor
where: Any ripperdoc from level 30. Tiers: 4 to 5++.
effect: Armor 88–108; −6–7% all damage taken.
verdict: For tanks from level 30.

name: Painducer
where: Any ripperdoc from level 30. Tiers: 4 to 5++.
effect: Armor 114–138; turns 25–30% of damage taken into damage over time (you take it gradually).
verdict: For builds that heal often and prefer damage spread out.

name: Peripheral Inverse
where: Dogtown ripperdocs (Phantom Liberty) and Airdrops: one of the 15 iconic implants the repeating Airdrops guarantee (they start in Lucretia My Reflection). Tiers: 4 to 5++.
effect: Iconic ProxiShield: Armor 8–36; −34–45% damage from enemies within 3 m, tapering to 0 at 6 m.
verdict: For Phantom Liberty melee builds.

name: ProxiShield
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: Armor 8–36; −8–20% damage from enemies within 3 m, tapering to 0 at 6 m.
verdict: For melee builds from the start.

name: RangeGuard
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: Armor 10–34; +30–90 Armor when no enemy is within 6 m.
verdict: For gunfighters and netrunners who fight at range.

name: Shock-n-Awe
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: Armor 44–92; when hit, 10% chance to release an electroshock (135–500 damage). Update 2.1 changed its attunement bonus to Tech weapon damage.
verdict: For Technical Ability builds who fight up close.

name: Subdermal Armor
where: Viktor installs it in The Ripperdoc: one of the three implants on the €$21,000 bill (if you don't pay, the debt opens Paid in Full). Later, any ripperdoc. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: Armor 17–49, nothing else. Chitin is its iconic version.
verdict: You have it from the start; replace it when something better comes along.

name: Basic Kiroshi Optics
where: Viktor installs them in The Ripperdoc, as part of the €$21,000 bill or debt. Later, any ripperdoc. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: −20–44% camera detection speed and 4–10× scan zoom. Before 2.0 these were the only optics (obsolete).
verdict: Starter optics; swap them for a pair with a real effect.

name: Behavioral Imprint-synced Faceplate
where: Farida Nazeri installs it in Birds with Broken Wings (Phantom Liberty); the same job unlocks the second Face slot. Not sold. Tiers: 5 only.
effect: Iconic. Activate it to change identity: out of combat it shakes off police up to 4 stars. Cooldown 1500 s. Used in I've Seen That Face Before. Costs 0 capacity.
verdict: For everyone playing Phantom Liberty: free and in its own slot.

name: Kiroshi "Clairvoyant" Optics
where: Any ripperdoc from level 20. Tiers: 3 to 5++. In Phantom Liberty a scripted Airdrop at Tranquil Terrace (Luxor Heights) holds one after Lucretia My Reflection. (The game files start it at Tier 1.)
effect: While scanning, highlights enemies within 12.5–19.5 m for 60 s; 6–10× zoom.
verdict: For stealth players who want to see enemies.

name: Kiroshi "Cockatrice" Optics
where: Dogtown ripperdocs (Phantom Liberty) from level 35 and Airdrops: one of the 15 iconic implants the repeating Airdrops guarantee (they start in Lucretia My Reflection). Tiers: 4 to 5++.
effect: Iconic optics: +25–35% Crit Chance; 10× zoom.
verdict: For Phantom Liberty crit builds.

name: Kiroshi "Doomsayer" Optics
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: While scanning, highlights explosives and traps within 10–29 m; 4–10× zoom.
verdict: For players exploring on foot who don't want to step on mines.

name: Kiroshi "Sentry" Optics
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: While scanning, highlights cameras and turrets within 15–39 m; 4–10× zoom. Intelligence-attuned.
verdict: The cheap early upgrade for a netrunner (inference).

name: Kiroshi "Stalker" Optics
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: Linked to a Tech weapon: highlights enemies behind cover while aiming; 4–10× zoom.
verdict: For Tech weapon builds that shoot through walls.

name: Kiroshi "The Oracle" Optics
where: Any ripperdoc from level 30. Tiers: 4 to 5++. (Sources disagree: the game files start it at Tier 1.)
effect: Sentry, Doomsayer and Clairvoyant combined: enemies (also behind cover), cameras and traps; 8–10× zoom.
verdict: The all-in-one optics for a level 30 stealth player.

name: Ballistic Coprocessor
where: Viktor installs it in The Ripperdoc, part of the €$21,000 bill. Later, any ripperdoc. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: Power weapons: more ricochets, +8–30% ricochet damage and a trajectory preview.
verdict: For Power weapon users who don't need Smart weapons.

name: Handle Wrap
where: Any ripperdoc from level 20. Tiers: 3 to 5++.
effect: Equipping or throwing a throwable: +8–27% Crit Chance with throwables for 6 s.
verdict: For throwing-knife builds.

name: Immovable Force
where: Dogtown ripperdocs (Phantom Liberty) from level 10 and Airdrops: one of the 15 iconic implants the repeating Airdrops guarantee (they start in Lucretia My Reflection). Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Iconic: −18–35% recoil, −25% spread, and cover bonuses always active with ranged weapons.
verdict: For assault rifle and LMG users.

name: Microgenerator
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Reloading an empty weapon makes the next shot release an electroshock (75–250 Electrical damage). Update 2.1 lowered its damage and capacity cost.
verdict: For gunfighters who empty the magazine.

name: Shock Absorber
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 1 to 5++. (Sources disagree: the game files start it at Tier 2.)
effect: −8–24% recoil.
verdict: For any gunfighter before Immovable Force.

name: Smart Link
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: Enables Smart weapon targeting; +10–20% lock duration, +5–15% Smart weapon Crit Damage and +1–2 Max RAM. The three tattoos do the same job for 0 capacity.
verdict: A must for Smart weapons if you don't have one of the tattoos.

name: Tattoo: Johnny's Special
where: Chippin' In, when you choose a tattoo with Cassius Ryder. Tiers: 1 to 5.
effect: Works as a Smart Link (enables Smart weapon targeting) and costs 0 capacity.
verdict: For Smart weapon users who want to save capacity.

name: Tattoo: Together Forever
where: Chippin' In, picking "The Other One" with Cassius Ryder. Tiers: 1 to 5.
effect: Works as a Smart Link (enables Smart weapon targeting) and costs 0 capacity.
verdict: For Smart weapon users who want to save capacity.

name: Tattoo: Tyger Claws Dermal Imprint
where: Wakako Okada's gift after The Gig: Cassius Ryder installs it for free. Tiers: 1 to 5++ (the game files start it at Tier 2).
effect: Works as a Smart Link; +10–20% lock-on speed and a smaller Smart reticle. Costs 0 capacity.
verdict: The best free early Smart Link for Smart weapons.

name: Adrenaline Booster
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: +10–25% Stamina on a melee kill.
verdict: For melee builds that run out of Stamina.

name: Biomonitor
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: Uses your health item automatically below 50% Health; +2–16% health item effect.
verdict: For anyone who forgets to heal mid-fight.

name: Black Mamba
where: Any ripperdoc from level 20. Tiers: 3 to 5++.
effect: Against Poisoned enemies: −90% Poison damage, but +10–22% all other damage.
verdict: For Poison builds that finish with another damage type.

name: Blood Pump
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Works as a health item: heals 45–110 Health, then 9–23 per second for 6 s.
verdict: An extra heal for any build.

name: Clutch Padding
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: −7–20% Stamina cost for shooting.
verdict: For gunfighters who keep shooting.

name: Electromag Recycler
where: Dogtown ripperdocs (Phantom Liberty) and Airdrops: one of the 15 iconic implants the repeating Airdrops guarantee (they start in Lucretia My Reflection). Tiers: 3 to 5++.
effect: Iconic Feedback Circuit: +2.5–5% Health and Stamina on a fully charged Tech weapon hit.
verdict: For Phantom Liberty Tech weapon builds.

name: Feedback Circuit
where: Any ripperdoc from level 20. Tiers: 3 to 5++.
effect: +1.5–3.5% Health on a fully charged Tech weapon hit.
verdict: For Tech weapon builds.

name: Heal-On-Kill
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: +3–7.5% Health per kill.
verdict: Passive healing for any build that kills often.

name: Isometric Stabilizer
where: Dogtown ripperdocs (Phantom Liberty) and Airdrops: one of the 15 iconic implants the repeating Airdrops guarantee (they start in Lucretia My Reflection). Tiers: 3 to 5++.
effect: Iconic: −13–20% Stamina cost for all attacks.
verdict: For Phantom Liberty builds that burn Stamina.

name: Microrotors
where: Any ripperdoc. Tiers: 1 to 5++. Lely Hein also carries one (Cyberpsycho Sighting: Six Feet Under, Northside).
effect: +10–25% melee attack speed. An unverified wiki note says that since 2.11 it does nothing for weapons with attack speed above 2.
verdict: For melee builds with slow weapons.

name: Second Heart
where: Any ripperdoc from level 30. Tiers: 4 to 5++.
effect: When your Health hits 0 you revive at 100%. Cooldown 300–220 s.
verdict: A second life for any build from level 30.

name: ThreatEvac
where: Any ripperdoc from level 1. Tiers: 1 to 5++.
effect: Movement speed rises as Health drops below 25% (up to +15–39%).
verdict: A cheap way to run away at low Health.

name: Fortified Ankles
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 1 to 5++. (Sources disagree: the game files start it at Tier 2.)
effect: Armor 35–103; hold jump to charge a high jump.
verdict: The alternative to double jump: a charged high jump and more Armor.

name: Jenkins' Tendons
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Armor 22; +30% sprint speed, tapering to +10% after 5 s. Leeroy Ligament System is its iconic version.
verdict: For players who cross the city on foot.

name: Leeroy Ligament System
where: Dogtown ripperdocs (Phantom Liberty) and Airdrops: one of the 15 iconic implants the repeating Airdrops guarantee (they start in Lucretia My Reflection). Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Iconic Jenkins' Tendons: Armor 10–26; +12–20% movement speed. Update 2.1 raised its Armor and cut its cost.
verdict: For fast Phantom Liberty builds.

name: Lynx Paws
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Armor 16–34; 50% quieter movement, +6–12% crouch speed and −20% fall damage (added in 2.1).
verdict: For stealth players.

name: Reinforced Tendons
where: Any ripperdoc from level 10. Tiers: 2 to 5++.
effect: Armor 20; double jump. Update 2.1 lowered its Armor. Fortified Ankles is the alternative (there is one Legs slot).
verdict: For almost everyone: double jump opens shortcuts all over the city (game8 calls it the best leg cyberware of 2.0).
